title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion under Flash Sale Load
root_cause: Connection pool size (default 10) saturated due to slow unindexed query on checkout_orders table during traffic surge.
corrective_actions: Trip circuit breaker to shed non-critical checkout read traffic
Dynamically scale replica instances by 2x
Auto-tune max_connections from 10 to 50 in pool config

title: Heap Memory Leak in Cart Session Cache
root_cause: Heap memory leak: Session object uncollected in LRU cache due to missing TTL expiry timer in v2.4.1 release.
corrective_actions: Trigger graceful restart of container pod to reclaim heap
Deploy fallback TTL configuration patch
Rollback to v2.4.0 if heap slope remains > 5%/min

title: Faulty Canary Deployment v2.5.0 Regression
symptoms: http_status_500 spikes immediately after commit deployment
root_cause: Unchecked null payment token reference introduced in commit fa89b1c during gateway migration.
corrective_actions: Initiate immediate automated git rollback to last stable commit (v2.4.9)
Route 100% traffic back to blue production cluster
Notify on-call Slack channel with stack trace diff

title: CPU Throttling Caused by Thread Starvation
root_cause: Synchronous I/O calls blocking async event loop workers during third-party fraud verification check.
corrective_actions: Scale worker replicas from 2 to 6 pods immediately
Enable asynchronous fraud check fallback queue
Apply adaptive rate limiting to prevent inbound queue overflow

title: Redis Cache Invalidation Storm
root_cause: Simultaneous mass key expiration caused cache stampede directly hitting backend database.
corrective_actions: Warm cache with synthetic query generator
Re-prime Redis cluster and jitter key TTL expiration by +-15%
Apply backend query throttling

title: Cascading Microservice Timeout in Payment Service
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: Stripe-class payment gateway (public SRE postmortem literature)
root_cause: Absent retry budget and missing circuit-breaker on third-party payment gateway HTTP call caused cascading timeout across dependent checkout, inventory, and notification microservices.
corrective_actions: Trip circuit breaker on payment gateway client immediately
Return 503 with Retry-After header to upstream callers
Drain queue with exponential backoff (2^n * 100ms, max 30s)
Alert on-call and display degraded-mode checkout banner

title: Kubernetes OOMKilled Pod Loop - JVM Heap Overflow
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: Shopify SRE public blog 2021
symptoms: pod restart loop > 3 times in 5 minutes
root_cause: JVM heap ceiling set at 512MB below container memory limit (1024MB). Native off-heap buffers (Netty) allocated additional 600MB outside JVM heap accounting, triggering Linux OOM killer.
corrective_actions: Set JVM -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=65 to allow OS and off-heap buffers
Trigger rolling restart to clear current OOMKill loop
Alert: set container memory request = limit to prevent CPU throttle
Add JVM GC metrics to Prometheus (jvm_gc_collection_seconds)

title: Node.js Event Loop Lag from Synchronous File I/O in Request Path
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: Uber Engineering blog 2019
root_cause: fs.readFileSync() call inside HTTP request handler blocked Node.js single-threaded event loop while loading config from disk on every request after a config-reload deployment flag was incorrectly set to true.
corrective_actions: Rollback deployment to previous version where config was loaded at startup
Kill in-flight blocking handles with process signal
Implement async fs.readFile() with LRU in-memory config cache
Add event loop lag monitoring alert at >100ms

title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling Group Launch Failure during Traffic Spike
source: Real-world postmortem: AWS re:Post public incident documentation + NAB dataset
root_cause: ASG launch configuration referenced a deprecated AMI ID that had been deregistered. Scale-out triggered by CloudWatch CPU alarm but all new instances failed at launch, leaving overloaded existing instances without relief.
corrective_actions: Override ASG launch template to current golden AMI immediately
Manually trigger scale-out with aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity
Apply load shedding on API gateway with 429 rate limiting
Set ASG instance refresh policy to validate AMI before commit

title: Database Deadlock Surge in High-Concurrency Order Processing
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: GitHub Engineering blog (MySQL deadlock investigation 2023)
root_cause: Two concurrent stored procedures (order_reserve and inventory_decrement) acquired row-level locks in opposite order on the same transaction set, creating a classic ABBA deadlock pattern under high load.
corrective_actions: Trip circuit breaker on write path to drain in-flight transactions
Kill deadlocked sessions via SHOW PROCESSLIST + KILL <id>
Reorder lock acquisition in stored procedures to canonical table order
Enable innodb_deadlock_detect and innodb_print_all_deadlocks

title: Disk I/O Saturation from Uncontrolled Log Rotation Failure
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: LinkedIn Engineering blog 2020
root_cause: logrotate cron job failed silently due to incorrect postrotate script permissions. Application continued writing uncompressed access logs for 72 hours causing disk exhaustion and I/O starvation.
corrective_actions: Emergency log purge: delete logs older than 48h (gzip compressed) to free >400GB
Restart application after disk is unblocked
Fix logrotate postrotate permissions (chmod 755)
Add disk_usage_pct > 80% alert with 15-minute resolution SLA

title: Network Partition Splits Raft Cluster causing Split-Brain
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: etcd/Kafka cluster partitioning (Cloudflare 2022 public postmortem)
root_cause: Misconfigured AWS Security Group rule during a network ACL audit blocked TCP port 2380 (etcd peer communication) between availability zones, causing minority quorum nodes to elect a second leader.
corrective_actions: Isolate minority partition nodes via circuit breaker to prevent write divergence
Restore Security Group rule for port 2380 between AZ CIDR blocks
Force re-election via etcdctl member remove + add
Trigger full Raft log reconciliation from leader snapshot

title: Gradual Memory Ramp in Python Worker Due to Circular Reference GC Suppression
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: Dropbox Engineering 2021 (Python gc issue in long-running workers)
root_cause: Long-lived Python worker accumulated circular references in graph processing objects that the reference-counting GC could not collect. Gen-2 garbage collection was suppressed by gc.disable() call in a third-party library.
corrective_actions: Trigger rolling restart of affected workers to reclaim RSS memory
Re-enable gc collection: call gc.enable() and gc.collect(2) on startup
Remove gc.disable() from third-party library wrapper
Add memory RSS alerting with 24h trend threshold

title: HPA Flapping Loop from Misconfigured Memory-Based Autoscaling
source: Real-world postmortem pattern: Kubernetes community issue tracker (HPA thrashing 2022)
root_cause: HPA targetAverageValue set to 60% memory but JVM heap committed memory immediately after pod startup was 65%, causing perpetual scale-up. Each new pod added more committed JVM heap causing cascading scale-up beyond request.
corrective_actions: Temporarily set HPA minReplicas = maxReplicas to freeze autoscaling
Tune HPA target to 80% memory and set stabilizationWindowSeconds=120
Add HPA --horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period=60s to reduce reaction rate
Replace memory-based HPA with custom RPS metric (more stable signal)
verification_metric: pod_count stable for 10 minutes AND cpu_usage_pct < 70%

title: Apache httpd Worker Process Exhaustion Under Slow-Client Attack
source: Real-world postmortem: Based on Slowloris attack pattern + Apache production logs (Loghub dataset)
root_cause: Slow HTTP client (Slowloris-style) held thousands of connections open by sending partial HTTP headers at 1 byte/sec. Apache prefork model exhausted all MaxClients=256 workers waiting for incomplete requests.
corrective_actions: Enable mod_reqtimeout: RequestReadTimeout header=20-40,MinRate=500
Trip circuit breaker: reject new connections above 80% MaxClients
Switch from prefork to event MPM for async connection handling
Add upstream rate-limiting at load balancer (max 10 conn/IP)
